newsitem.title: PERU: LIMA SHRS END DOWN AS FOREIGNERS REMAIN SIDELINED.
newsitem.headline: LIMA SHRS END DOWN AS FOREIGNERS REMAIN SIDELINED.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed slightly down Tuesday as foreign investors continued to look for gains in other markets in the region, while local players bought brewery stocks and sold miners, brokers said.
With foreigners focusing on the New York and Mexican stock exchanges, local selective buying would again likely dominate the Lima bolsa Wednesday, they added.

Tuesday, the General Index fell 0.23 percent to 2,055.6 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index dipped 0.19 percent to 2,956.8 points. In a total of 1,864 trades, volume was 41.0 million soles ($15.5 million).

"The brewers are doing well because of the economy's growth. The rise is more noticeable because mining stocks are seeing a slight fall as zinc future prices appear weak," Carlos Patron of Peruval said.
Peru's largest brewery UCP Backus rose 1.28 percent to 2.38 soles on the day's highest volume of 878,000 shares.
Leading polymetallic miner Atacocha fell 1.87 percent to close at 2.63 soles on volume of 208,000 shares.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru edged up 0.16 percent to 6.40 soles on volume of 700,000 shares.
